items.summary: The author, who builds apps daily for a Hulry newsletter called Wonder Tools, recommends seven iOS and macOS applications. Dia is presented as a clean browser with optional AI features that the writer switched to after their previous browser glitched; it costs $10 per month on an optional plan. CleanShot is described as a screenshot tool used by the author for more than seven years.
items.title: Seven iOS and macOS apps recommended for downloading now

items.summary: In a weekly market review, ST's business correspondents explain this week's Singapore moves. The three major banks fell: DBS shares dropped 3.78% after net profit missed estimates and fell 5% to $2.81 billion; UOB slid 10.27% despite an 182% jump in third-quarter profit to $1.25 billion, though it still missed the $1.38 billion consensus; OCBC fell 4.28% even as net earnings rose 3% to $2.04 billion. Elsewhere, SATS dropped about 3% after work pass concerns at Changi Airport, and Grab raised its full-year guidance on strong results. The US midterm tech rout sent the Nasdaq 100 down 5.52%, with Singapore's STI ending the week lower too.
items.title: Singapore banks and tech stocks slide amid weak earnings

items.summary: The collapse of AI-related trades after US midterm elections is prompting investors to diversify away from semiconductor-heavy positions toward out-of-favour Chinese and Indian equities. Rajeev De Mello of Gama Asset Management expects broader investment dispersion, while LOGOS Asset Management shifted holdings into Indian tech and financial firms following October sales in SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. India’s Nifty 50 gained 8.6% last week on foreign inflows totalling US$1.9 billion (S$2.4 billion) through Nov 4, aided by lower oil prices. Caution persists as some investors maintain AI sell-offs may continue despite longer-term growth prospects. BLOOMBERG
items.title: AI Sell-Off Revives China and India Stocks

items.summary: A UK news report examines a wave of cyber incidents, opening with fruit wholesaler Alex Pearce discovering his London refrigeration units overheating after he cut the internet cable. On 30 October Binance lost $6.3bn (£4.7bn) in a record crypto heist, and on 1 November hackers sent Kyiv a fake nuclear alert; retailers across seven European countries reported fridges reaching up to 50C (122F). The National Cyber Security Centre’s Richard Horne called it the “foothills” of a new hacking landscape. Ciaran Martin disputed comparisons to China’s Wuhan moment, citing prior attacks such as WannaCry in 2017 and Finland’s nearly 21,000 incidents by 2022. Experts note AI is surfacing vulnerabilities while actual breaches have not matched that surge.
items.title: UK Cyber Agency Warns of Rising Hacking Wave Amid Fridge Hack and Crypto Heist

items.summary: Nous Research has released Arete-27B, a supervised fine-tune of Alibaba’s open-weight Qwen3.8-27B model that removes Chinese state framing from answers. On Nous’s own 803-prompt evaluation, the share of propaganda-laden responses fell to about 0.9%, down from 22% for the base model, while fact recall rose to 2.98 out of 5. The team used no reinforcement learning or preference optimization; training covered roughly 52.8 million tokens at a 64k context using an open teacher called Inkling from Thinking Machines. Nous states that capability held on its benchmarks and the weights, eval set and training data are all public under Apache 2.0 and MIT licenses. Fact score still trails peers, with 216 of 803 answers scoring zero.
items.title: Nous Research Releases Arete-27B to Strip Qwen of State Framing

items.summary: This system-design refresher outlines six commonly used orchestration frameworks in AI systems, describing how each manages tasks across agents. LangGraph uses graph-based state transitions; CrewAI assigns roles to sequential or manager-driven agents; Microsoft Agent Framework adds branching, checkpoints, and human pauses; OpenAI Agents SDK lets an LLM decide delegation versus self-execution; Google ADK splits work between a developer-defined strategy and root agent; Claude Agent SDK runs orchestration inside the agent itself. The episode also lists six cost-optimization techniques: prompt caching, model routing, batch API requests, semantic cache, trimmed context, and smaller models via distillation or quantization. It closes with two discussion prompts for listeners.
items.title: Six AI Orchestration Frameworks and Cost-Saving Strategies Explained

items.summary: The Egyptian government is accelerating plans to develop its oil and gas resources, targeting a production capacity of 6.6 billion cubic feet per day by 2027 through increased drilling, exploration incentives, and investment from international majors. Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi discussed the agenda at an October roundtable with Cypriot officials and executives. The government aims to connect new discoveries to existing infrastructure while addressing challenges in partnership with partners; production has fallen due to ageing Mediterranean fields such as Zohr. President Abdel Fattah Al-Sisi announced plans to double crude output under a five-year strategy, including over $4 billion for six refineries. Eni, which invested around $8.5 billion and produced approximately 242,000 bpd in 2025, plans further drilling and gas processing expansion.
items.title: Egypt Pursues Billions in Investment to Revive Oil and Gas Output

items.summary: CleanTechnica reviewed the Velotric GoMad Electric Utility e-bike, which it calls a flexible jack-of-all-trades model. The review bike arrived in obsidian and tested well with an optional passenger kit rated for 500 pounds. It is listed at $1,899 with a Black Friday offer including a free young passenger kit.
items.title: CleanTechnica Reviews Velotric GoMad Utility E-Bike

items.summary: Esbjerg, Denmark is testing large electric heat pumps that pull warmth from the North Sea to feed its district-heating network. A two-hour winter test saw seawater enter at 3.3°C and leave at 1.2°C while the pumps drew 19.9 MW of electricity to deliver 55.2 MW of heat, with 35.3 MW coming from the cold water itself. The team’s May 2025 operating report recorded a coefficient of performance of 2.8, though that figure reflects only the short test and was below earlier expectations before full guarantee testing finished. Esbjerg uses carbon dioxide refrigerant as part of replacing its retired coal plant. Costs depend on electricity prices and network temperatures, and emissions cuts cannot be fully credited to this system alone.
items.title: Esbjerg Tests Cold Seawater Heat Pumps for District Heating

items.summary: An IndiGo flight from Bengaluru bound for Lucknow returned to Kempegowda International Airport on Saturday evening after a handwritten note threatening a hijack was found in the aircraft's lavatory, triggering an emergency and security sweep. The threat was later declared a hoax, and the plane resumed its journey.
items.title: IndiGo Flight Returns After Hijack Threat Note Found in Lavatory

items.summary: Alberto De Negri, Head of Advisory for Healthcare at KPMG's Europe, Middle East and Africa practice, told Business Today that the growing flow of private equity capital into India's healthcare sector could increase treatment costs unless clear regulations and a public-private cooperation framework are in place. He said investors expect returns within roughly five years and seek predictable revenues and stable operating conditions. De Negri cautioned against excessive competition between public and private providers, warning it may raise procedures without improving outcomes. He advocated regulatory oversight by governments while the private sector contributes efficiency and technology, and urged India to invest beyond hospitals in primary care, community services and home-based treatment.
items.title: KPMG Executive Warns Private Equity May Raise India Healthcare Costs

items.summary: A young fan named Kai said Pokemon cards are being hyped “like crypto,” which he blames for driving up prices and pushing out collectors. At a London store, Forbidden Planet, queues stretched past 120 people before the Friday opening; staff limit high-demand products like the £49.99 Delta Reign elite trainer box to one per customer and use an unsealing policy that blocks reselling opened stock. Calvin Innes said demand has “outrun the machines,” while Pokémon still makes about 10bn cards a year, because supply stays capped. Parents report ugly buying experiences and are seeking advice online; some shops now run free kids clubs to keep product for players rather than buyers.
items.title: Pokemon Card Fans Face Scalpers and Long Queues

items.summary: Mike Fries, boss of co-owner Liberty Global, said this week the company is not in crisis despite swingeing job cuts, a £22bn debt pile and loss of hundreds of thousands of customers. The UK telecoms firm announced £800m in cost savings, including potentially cutting up to a quarter of its 16,000 UK staff. In two years it lost 182,000 broadband and 644,000 mobile customers. A surprise O2 bill increase estimated cost about 110,000 customers. Industry watchers point to operational execution problems and fierce competition; the company says complaints have fallen sharply.
items.title: Virgin Media O2 weighs up job cuts amid £22bn debt and customer losses

items.summary: The China International Import Expo 2026 presented semiconductor firms from raw materials to AI servers on one floor. Organizers say the rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving new demand across the industry, with each supply-chain part playing a vital role as global tech companies show how their operations in China connect with the wider Asia-Pacific region.
items.title: Semiconductor Firms Deepen China Ties at CIIE 2026

items.summary: CGTN spoke with Liam Corkery, who is debuting new beauty products at the China International Import Expo. The article notes that while New Zealand is renowned for agricultural products worldwide, its beauty products are gaining popularity in China following the introduction of a new protocol.
items.title: New Zealand Beauty Products Enter China Market Through New Protocol

items.summary: Australian researcher Saul Justin Newman argues that “blue zones” — regions said to hold exceptional longevity — rest on weak evidence, citing low scientific proof and high conflicts of interest among those who study them. In his 2026 book Morbid: Debunking Modern Longevity Science (2026), he contends extraordinary claims about people past 100 stem more from unreliable birth records than genetics or diet. Newman notes that roughly a quarter of the world’s children lack birth certificates, undermining age verification. He points to cases where centenarians were “only alive on paper,” and criticizes commercial certification schemes priced between $3 million and $40 million. In an EL PAÍS interview he says increasing average lifespan matters more than chasing mythical longevity places.
items.title: Researcher Questions Reliability of Blue Zones and Longevity Claims

items.summary: Military attachés from about 50 countries watched a helicopter flight training demonstration on Friday at the PLA Army Aviation Institute. The pilots showcased maneuvers at different speeds, impressing foreign military representatives with their skills and precision.
items.title: Foreign Military Attachés Impressed by PLA Helicopter Flight Show

items.summary: At the 9th China International Import Expo (CIIE), international exhibitors are meeting Chinese buyers in a series of 15-minute sessions. From Italian egg pasta and French food supplements to South African sauces, businesses from across the globe seek opportunities to enter the Chinese market. With more than 150 buyers registered, including JINGDONG and Tsingtao Brewery, these brief encounters may lead to larger business deals.
items.title: CIIE Launches Business Speed Dating for Global Exhibitors and Chinese Buyers

items.summary: Senator Matt Canavan supports Australia staying in the Paris Agreement, which he says covers only having a policy to reduce emissions and reporting against it. He opposes an EU free trade deal that would legally bind the country to net zero by 2050, calling it a backdoor way to force stronger commitments beyond what Parliament signed up to. Canavan said he texted Trade Minister Don Farrell to discuss details constructively while warning the pact could harm dairy farmers and critical minerals exporters.
items.title: Canavan backs Paris deal but rejects EU trade pact climate bind

items.summary: Usman Khawaja denied on Sunday that he had thrown anyone under the bus, responding to an excerpt from his autobiography claiming the entire Australian team knew of ball tampering during a 2018 South Africa tour. Only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were banned in Sandpapergate. Khawaja said these three took blame for all and deserve justice.
items.title: Khawaja denies throwing teammates under the bus over ball-tampering scandal

items.summary: The New Zealand duo of Jordie Barrett and Will Jordan may be unavailable for next weekend's Nations Championship match against Wales, having been injured at Murrayfield in Saturday's 43-21 All Blacks victory over Scotland. Barrett failed a head injury assessment following contact with Blair Kinghorn, while Jordan sustained a suspected hamstring problem.
items.title: New Zealand pair could miss Wales clash after injuries

items.summary: A prolonged cloudy, windless spell could trigger Europe’s first ‘dunkelflaute’ of the year, throttling solar and wind output and pushing energy prices higher. German day-ahead power prices for 29 October were above €300 per megawatt-hour under Bloomberg forecasts, roughly double the October average, with evening peaks exceeding €500. A UK resident whose home has 12 panels (6.36 kW capacity) told Euronews Earth that output fell to 10.90 kWh on Wednesday and just 2.40 kWh on Thursday’s overcast day, while importing 27.40 kWh and then 20.60 kWh; the resident said they were ‘hardly producing any power’ but expect recovery as clouds clear. Solar’s EU share of generation fell from 25.4 per cent in June to 13.2 per cent in October, though Good Energy says UK home systems can still yield around 25-35 per cent of annual output in winter, and hydropower has begun rising to compensate.
items.title: Europe’s Solar Boom Faces a Cloudy Winter Test

items.summary: A new survey by Preply, an online language-learning marketplace, examined public data and responses from 1,600 people across 27 countries about European etiquette. The findings challenged common assumptions: in 23 of the 27 countries, most respondents would wait for a host to initiate two cheek kisses rather than offer them first. Shoe removal is expected in 24 of those countries, with Spain, Italy and Portugal as exceptions. Finishing one's meal was seen as respectful across all 27 countries, though 82% of men always did so versus 75% of women. Punctuality preferences varied widely by country and gender. Preply noted that searches for etiquette guidance rose sharply in the past year.
items.title: Survey Reveals Etiquette Rules Travellers Should Know Before Heading to Europe

items.summary: Snow fell across parts of New South Wales after a strong cold front swept through the state, dropping temperatures and bringing rain and storms. Suburbs that reached 30 degrees Celsius on Saturday cooled by more than 10C by evening. A Thredbo local described the snow as beautiful but unexpected following a warm winter.
items.title: Unexpected Snow Blankets Parts of NSW Ahead of Summer

items.summary: Activists warn that deporting two more Uyghurs from Thailand would put their lives in grave danger, with one man saying he would be “like a slave” if sent back. Thai authorities last year forcibly deported 40 Uyghur men despite pleas and UN objections; the US and Canada reportedly offered resettlement, but Bangkok avoided upsetting Beijing. The two men had served seven years for an attempted escape in January 2020. Human Rights Watch’s Elaine Pearson called for safe third-country travel, citing past disappearances after deportations.
items.title: Uyghur Deportees Warn of Slavery in China

items.summary: Snow fell across parts of NSW, Victoria and Tasmania during an unseasonal cold snap through the region in November. The Bureau of Meteorology forecast the event as a system drawing cold air from Antarctica lowered apparent temperatures below 13C in five capital cities at midday. Warmer conditions are expected Monday to Tuesday.
items.title: Unseasonal cold blast brings springtime snow across Australia's south-east

items.summary: Mary Austin, Freddie Mercury's longtime partner who inherited his Garden Lodge home in west London, discusses preserving his memory through her 2024 book A Life in Lyrics. She describes their relationship from 1970 to 1977, when they lived together for nearly eight years while she worked as his personal assistant and covered household expenses. Austin says the love was more powerful than she realized, and notes Mercury died of AIDS in November 1991 before leaving her his possessions.
items.title: Freddie Mercury's former fiancée reflects on their love and legacy

items.summary: Fans of the Japanese drama "Vivant" are increasingly visiting Azerbaijan to see filming locations, a trend travel agencies call "set-jetting." Visitors like Mayumi Kishi from Tokyo have traveled specifically for these sites. Travel packages tied to the show's second season already have waiting lists.
items.title: Azerbaijan Sees Rise in Japanese 'Set-Jetting' Tourism Over Vivant Drama

items.summary: A strong 5.7-magnitude earthquake struck central Japan early Sunday, injuring dozens and disrupting train services, officials and local media said. It hit Shizuoka Prefecture at 1:04 am; no tsunami warning was issued and there were no reported deaths. Aichi authorities received 16 reports of mostly minor injuries, while neighboring regions counted at least 24 hurt. The quake also damaged windows and shelves across Toyohashi and Toyota cities in Aichi, delayed Shinkansen services, and was felt as far west as Osaka. No immediate serious damage or injuries were reported from a separate 4.3-magnitude quake that struck Kumamoto later Sunday.
items.title: Magnitude 5.7 Quake Injures Dozens in Central Japan

items.summary: During his second day in Uruguay, Pope Leo XIV addressed young people at Montevideo's Estadio Centenario and spoke with academics at the Catholic University of Uruguay. He urged them to embrace family life and real human contact over digital isolation, called for wise use of artificial intelligence in education, encouraged marriage amid growing secularization, and visited a poor neighborhood where he stressed protecting vulnerable children. The visit continued with an open-air mass attended by 40,000 faithful.
items.title: Pope Leo XIV Urges Uruguayan Youth on Family, Human Connection

items.summary: A Nov. 8 news roundup reports Poland's Interior Minister Marcin Kierwinski says a far-right ideology may have influenced the central Krakow attacker; six were killed including one foreign national while 16 were injured. It also notes Israeli President Isaac Herzog named Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government, and that US Central Command announced Task Force Iron Gate on Nov. 7 to disrupt Iran's land supply routes.
items.title: Morning Briefing Covers Krakow Attack, Israel Government Task and US-Iran Pressure

items.summary: Italian Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani says cyber-criminals have been publishing his personal data on the dark web and targeting his family, he said in a post on X. He attributed the attacks to Italy's support for Ukraine, calling defending democracy dangerous to these criminal entities. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni blamed pro-Russian hackers and offered her full solidarity.
items.title: Italy's Foreign Minister Says Hackers Leaked His Personal Data Over Ukraine Stance

items.summary: Michel Barnier, the EU's former Brexit negotiator, told BBC's Laura Kuenssberg that the UK cannot cherry pick which elements of the single market to adopt. He said there is no à la carte menu and that members would insist on conditions such as free movement of people. Burnham has suggested exploring closer ties with Europe since becoming prime minister in July, though he ruled out major changes before the next election. Barnier also predicted EU countries would reject reinstating the financial rebate first negotiated in 1985. Farage called him arrogant and a bully.
items.title: Barnier Warns UK Cannot Pick Single Market Elements

items.summary: Tanzania's opposition Chadema party called Friday a 'victorious day' after a court found its leader Tundu Lissu not guilty of treason. He was instead sentenced to four years for inciting unrest, a charge the article notes was absent from the case and that could bar him from the 2030 election if upheld. Chadema plans to appeal and seek bail. British and EU lawmakers called the charges politically motivated; Lissu described the trial as 'political persecution.' Tanzania's government puts post-election deaths at 518, versus thousands cited by rights groups.
items.title: Chadema Hails Victory After Lissu Acquitted of Treason

items.summary: This Global Voices interview spotlights EkoGard, a Montenegro organization working with the Digital Spark granting scheme to make its country cleaner. The article notes that although UNECE found progress toward EU alignment by 2028, recycling stays under 2 percent versus an EU target of 50 percent. Founder Senad Pepić explains how illegal dumpsites led EkoGard to build EkoMapa, a tool mapping environmental conditions settlement by settlement. Thomas Waitz praised recent landfill closures while warning more remain. The organization plans to share findings with local government and help launch a National Eco Line for reporting problems.
items.title: Montenegro Grantees Clean Up Waste Through Digital Tools and Community Action

items.summary: This step-by-step guide explains how users can use ChatGPT to create customised Diwali 2026 images, wishes, and greeting cards for sharing on WhatsApp. It offers two methods: generating festive pictures through the app's image feature or writing personalised greetings via chat prompts. The article provides five example image designs with specific visual elements like glowing diyas and rangoli patterns, plus tips to specify format, keep messages short, personalise content, try different styles, and review before sending. Author Swati Gandhi is a digital journalist covering international and geopolitical issues at Live Mint.
items.title: ChatGPT Guide for Creating Diwali Images and Wishes on WhatsApp

items.summary: Livemint—News Desk published an online, step-by-step guide on using Google Gemini to create customised Diwali 2026 images and wishes for WhatsApp. The article argues that personalised messages beat generic forwarded greetings flooding inboxes, then shows how a clear prompt about tone, recipient and length produces original text and high-resolution visuals. It pairs matching prompts so each family member receives an individual greeting this festive season. An example prompt asks for a 40-word professional wish; the AI returns a seven-line message ending with candle emojis.
items.title: Livemint publishes a step-by-step guide to creating Diwali greetings with Gemini AI

items.summary: Apple executive chairman Tim Cook wished people worldwide a happy Diwali on social media platform X, sharing a festive photograph he said was taken with an iPhone 18 Pro Max. The image shows a woman's hands holding bright diyas amid decorations. Cook credited the photo to Gursimran Basra and captioned it 'Shot on iPhone 18 Pro Max.' Apple frames the greeting around its camera capabilities, noting features like Enhanced Night mode, improved portrait photography, high-resolution processing, and computational photography that preserve highlights and realistic skin tones in low light. The post ties the festival celebration to the device's photographic strengths rather than presenting independent verification of any claim about image quality or performance.
items.title: Apple's Tim Cook Wishes Happy Diwali via iPhone Photo

items.summary: Elon Musk announced Tesla will add an extra production shift to clear the outstanding Cybertruck order backlog before dismantling the line around June/July next year, when it plans to expand Cybercab robotaxi production. The move follows earlier statements that Tesla would wind down Cybertruck output at its Texas factory and redirect resources toward the Cybercab as part of Musk's push into autonomous vehicles. Sales data cited by Kelley Blue Book shows US sales fell from nearly 39,000 in 2024 to about 20,000 last year, well below an initial prediction of 250,000 annual sales.
items.title: Tesla Adds Extra Cybertruck Shift Before Line Closes for Cybercab Expansion

items.summary: Microsoft is winding down its rental of computing capacity from Oracle after declining to renew the contract, part of a broader reassessment of billions in cloud partnerships. People familiar with the matter said the rented hardware used older-generation Nvidia chips and no longer fit Microsoft’s specifications; an Oracle spokesperson called demand for its infrastructure strong. The arrangement was announced in 2023 to power an AI-assisted version of Bing search, and Microsoft has committed more than $80 billion overall to rent capacity from other cloud companies as it re-thinks strategy amid high costs and delays.
items.title: Microsoft Ends Oracle AI Cloud Rental as It Cuts Back on Outsourced Capacity

items.summary: UK and Australian campaign groups CEASE and Collective Shout released a report alleging that OnlyFans creators use lifestyle videos on TikTok, including makeup tutorials and pet clips, to attract young audiences toward adult content. The report claims some creators bypass moderation using coded language such as 'corn' for 'porn'. Researchers warn these portrayals may encourage teenage girls to see the sex industry as an attractive career.
items.title: Campaign Groups Accuse TikTok of Promoting Sex Industry to Young Girls

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi extended Diwali greetings on Sunday and said he was traveling to Bastar to celebrate with security personnel. He posted messages wishing everyone happiness, peace and prosperity, praising the forces' sacrifices in an area where Naxalism once prevailed but development now flourishes. Modi also met Vice President C.P. Radhakrishnan and shared a Hindi message describing Diwali as symbolizing resolve against darkness.
items.title: Modi extends Diwali wishes, heads to Bastar for security forces

items.summary: Adani Enterprises Ltd plans annual capital expenditure of between ₹35,000 crore and ₹40,000 crore over the next couple of years. Finance head Manan Vakharia said during the earnings call that they may be somewhere in the range of ₹35,000 crore to ₹40,000 crore as airports, data centres and a proposed PVC complex lead expansion. The group reported its highest-ever half-year EBITDA of ₹11,958 crore for six months ended September 2026, up 56 per cent; consolidated income rose 62 per cent to ₹71,569 crore while profit before tax from continuing operations increased 45 per cent to ₹3,297 crore.
items.title: Adani Enterprises Sets ₹35,000-40,000 Crore Annual Capex for Two Years

items.summary: Shri Lal Krishna Advani entered his hundredth year of life on 8 November, a date that coincided with Diwali and marked anniversaries including the Jana Sangh's founding and RSS centenary. Born in Sindh in 1927, he rebuilt after Partition and strengthened both the Jana Sangh and BJP, whose rise saw Congress fall from 400 to below 200 seats by 1989. He served as Minister for Information and Broadcasting and Home Minister under the Janata Government of 1977. The people of India conferred the Bharat Ratna on him in 2024, as he enters his centenary year.
items.title: Lal Krishna Advani Enters Hundredth Year

items.summary: Jaypal posted on X that he was disgusted by what he called a racist display, saying the Hindu community should feel safe celebrating. Businessman Ajay Jain Bhutoria called it pure bigotry and said racial slurs against Hindus had no place in America. The Coalition of Hindus of North America advised members to stay vigilant. Jake Lang and Thomas Allen disrupted the event; Lang runs White Replacement and was pardoned by President Donald Trump on his second presidency's first day in 2025, after a January 6 2021 Capitol attack for which he served four years in jail.
items.title: Indian American Leaders Condemn Disruption of Seattle Diwali Celebration

items.summary: Meta Platforms Inc. launched a $25 billion bond offering on Tuesday Nov. 3, during the US midterms, betting that an election-day quiet would ease financing for its AI spending. The timing may have helped: by Wednesday Meta raised another €9 billion in its first euro debt sale after drawing record orders of €53 billion. But it did not borrow cheaply; notes due in 2056 priced at a yield premium of 2.2 percentage points above Treasuries, nearly 0.9 point wider than an April note. S&P Global Ratings had put Meta’s AA- outlook on negative the week before. Money managers warn hyperscalers now face higher premiums and must clarify how AI capital expenditure turns into revenue as a Democratic majority could slow data center development.
items.title: Meta Times Its Bond Sale on Election Day Amid Tech Debt Fears

items.summary: At an Aaj Tak Panchayat event, Yogi Adityanath said Akhilesh Yadav should apologise to devotees for defaming the Ram Mandir. The item is a developing story and will be updated.
items.title: Yogi Adityanath Urges Apology Over Ram Mandir Remarks

items.summary: Delhi's air quality worsened to severe on Diwali morning due to weather conditions and stubble burning, with measures limiting construction and firecracker use. Separately, Prime Minister Modi visited the Bastar region of Chhattisgarh to celebrate Diwali with security personnel, continuing his yearly tradition while underlining efforts against Left-Wing Extremism and development in previously affected areas.
items.title: Modi Celebrates Diwali in Bastar Amid Delhi Air Quality Concerns

items.summary: A woman rescued in Fargo, North Dakota, allegedly was chained to a bed for two years by her ex-husband Arturo Calzada-Becerril and his girlfriend Erendira Amoles. Police said she was restrained with a chain and padlock secured to the bedframe, beaten and sexually assaulted. Both were charged with kidnapping on November 6; bail is set at $500,000 each.
items.title: Ex-Husband Charged in Two-Year Captivity of Fargo Woman

items.summary: A Jawaharlal Nehru University student, Ajay, allegedly attacked a fellow second-year language student with a meat cleaver over his friendship with a woman student. Police said the victim sustained severe injuries and lost vision in his right eye after being rushed to AIIMS Trauma Centre. Based on her complaint, police registered an FIR under attempt-to-murder sections; no arrest had been made by Saturday evening. The Proctor's Office rusticated four students under Sections 32(1) and 32(3) of the JNU Act, 1966, barring them from campus pending inquiry.
items.title: JNU Student Blinded After Cleaver Attack Over Friendship With Woman

items.summary: Police said four members of a family were killed when a fire broke out at Sk Nizam Uddin's house in Jajpur district on Saturday evening. A short circuit is suspected but the cause remains to be ascertained.
items.title: Four Family Members Killed in Odisha Fire, Short Circuit Suspected

items.summary: A strong earthquake struck central Japan early Sunday, injuring at least 22 people and shattering store windows near Aichi and Shizuoka Prefectures. Local media reported the injuries, while Japan's Meteorological Agency rated the quake magnitude 5.7 and the US Geological Survey magnitude 5.5. Authorities warned of possible strong aftershocks in coming days and advised residents to watch for mudslides and falling rocks.
items.title: Magnitude 5.7 Earthquake Injures 22 in Central Japan

items.summary: Srinagar National Conference MP Aga Syed Ruhullah Mehdi resigned from the party and Lok Sabha on Tuesday, keeping a September promise. The 48-year-old cleric-politician said he felt at peace shunning his seat after a speech attacking President Farooq Abdullah and Chief Minister Omar Abdullah over their failure to restore Jammu and Kashmir's special status since August 2019. His resignation ends nearly two-and-a-half decades with the party amid growing voter frustration, though some fear it fragments the Muslim vote base. Ruhullah hinted at forming a new political group but faces an uphill task convincing Kashmiris his politics is organic. The article urges New Delhi to read his exit as a warning and engage with Kashmir's anxieties over autonomy.
items.title: Delhi urged to heed MP Ruhullah's Kashmir resignation

items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will celebrate Diwali on Sunday alongside security forces deployed in Chhattisgarh's Bastar, a region freed from Naxalism. In a post on X, he said: 'Heading to Bastar to celebrate Diwali with our brave security forces.' He added that development is now flourishing there and that he would continue the tradition of celebrating with soldiers each year. The government declared an end to Naxalism on March 31 this year (PTI).
items.title: Modi to Celebrate Diwali with Security Forces in Bastar

items.summary: In the U19 Asia Cup 2026 Group A match between arch-rivals Pakistan and India, Pakistan pacer Ali Raza struck twice at the crease. He dismissed opener VK Vineeth with a bouncer and bowled India U19 captain Lakshya Raichandani for a two-ball duck after a poor leave let the ball hit the top of off stump. India won the toss and elected to bat first.
items.title: Pakistan U19 dismiss India captain early in Asia Cup clash

items.summary: As veteran BJP leader L. K. Advani turned 100, Prime Minister Narendra Modi published a heartfelt article across national dailies honoring his "everlasting contribution to India." Writing on X and in the piece, Modi recalled Advani's role in strengthening the Jana Sangh and building the BJP, noting that during his tenures as party president the Congress fell from 400 seats to below 200 by 1989. He highlighted Advani's ideological clarity, intellectual sharpness, administrative record, opposition leadership, and involvement in the Somnath-to-Ayodhya Rath Yatra. Modi also paid tribute to Advani's wife Kamla and his personal qualities as a reader and Sindhi culture enthusiast. The article was auto-generated from an agency feed without editorial changes.
items.title: Modi Marks Advani's Centenary With Political Tribute

items.summary: As veteran BJP leader L.K. Advani turned 100, Prime Minister Narendra Modi published a tribute on X and in national dailies, recalling Partition, the Emergency, the Rath Yatra and Advani's role in building the party. Writing that as a youngster in 1947 Advani rebuilt his life 'without bitterness,' Modi said this shaped his work strengthening the Jana Sangh and BJP. Modi noted Advani served as BJP National President for three terms from 1986 to 1990, 1993 to 1998 and 2004 to 2005, making him the longest-serving president since the party's inception in 1980. He credited Advani with BJP rising as the single largest party in 1996 after Congress fell from 400 to below 200 seats in 1989, and said Advani was conferred Bharat Ratna by President Droupadi Murmu in March this year.
items.title: Modi marks LK Advani's centenary, credits him for shaping BJP

items.summary: On Sunday's Diwali morning, Delhi woke to thick smog with air quality in the 'Very Poor' category across several parts of the capital. India Gate recorded an AQI of 398 as per the CPCB, close to the severe threshold above 400. While the city average had not crossed that level, large areas already faced pollution at that stage.
items.title: Delhi-NCR Air Quality Nears Severe Level on Diwali Morning

items.summary: The Maharashtra State Road Transport Corporation (MSRTC) has extended the deadline for mandatory National Common Mobility Card registration by women passengers to 1 January 2027. Transport Minister Pratap Sarnaik announced on Friday that eligible women can keep discounted fares until 31 December 2026 without the smart card, after rural registrations stayed incomplete and users reported difficulties registering or using cards. Around 1.1 crore cards have been issued so far. MSRTC plans a registration drive with local officials to finish 100 per cent by year-end.
items.title: MSRTC Pushes NCMC Registration Deadline for Women Passengers

items.summary: The Commissioner of Railway Safety for the Western Circle completed a two-day safety inspection of the 44 km Tihi-Dhar rail section, conducted by E Srinivas over 5 and 6 November. Officials carried out speed trials reaching 120 kmph to assess track quality. The inspection flagged drainage improvements at bridges and replacement of bridge bearings before passenger services can begin. Services are expected by late November or December 2026.
items.title: CRS Approves Speed Trials on Tihi-Dhar Rail Link as Indore-Dahod Project Advances
